  <section class="bs-laser-project-notes" aria-labelledby="turkey-design-title">
    <p class="bs-laser-kicker">What the build shows</p>
    <h2 id="turkey-design-title">The SVG becomes a standing object</h2>
    <ul>
      <li>The large feather piece creates the broad silhouette and supports the visual identity of the turkey.</li>
      <li>The body and neck intersect the feather assembly instead of relying on a flat printed image.</li>
      <li>The feet and lower geometry keep the assembled figure upright on a tabletop.</li>
      <li>Engraved feather arcs and radial lines add detail without creating more loose parts.</li>
    </ul>
  </section>

  <section class="bs-laser-project-warning" aria-labelledby="turkey-fit-title">
    <p class="bs-laser-kicker">Fit before a full cut</p>
    <h2 id="turkey-fit-title">The slot must match the measured sheet</h2>
    <p>The original forum author reports using 1/8-inch “medium” draftboard and warns that the slots may need adjustment for other material. Measure the actual sheet, cut a small slot coupon first and revise the SVG before cutting the full turkey.</p>
    <p>The supplied SVG document is 9 × 4 inches and contains colour-separated Feathers, Text and Blue layers. Confirm which colours are cut, scored or engraved in the local laser workflow before sending the job.</p>
  </section>
